messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] decode-stream pool 'decode-7' seeing repeated CUDA OOMs and container restarts. Error-rate on /v1/decode/stream jumped to ~18% and request drops observed. Affected zone: us-west-2. Triggered paging at 2111111111.

aj (oncall): I'm on it. paging ack. pulling logs + checking oncall runbook. tagging eng-sre and eng-runtime.

jamal (eng-sre): seeing the same on logs — lots of `cudaOutOfMemoryError` during token decode loop. stack trace attached in the log stream. sample from node decode-7:```
2026-03-10T12:03:24Z ERROR runtime.decode worker-12: CUDA out of memory. tried to allocate 8.2GiB (GPU 0)
2026-03-10T12:03:24Z ERROR runtime.decode worker-12: Traceback (most recent call last): ... torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory.
2026-03-10T12:03:24Z INFO  gateway.request id=req_9f3a tokens_requested=120000 tokens_streamed=114532
```

maria (eng-runtime): @jamal can you grep for `tokens_requested` and `max_tokens` in the request traces? my hunch: a runaway generation / client override bypassed the gateway cap and sent huge max_tokens or left it unset -> model tried to decode until it hit OOM. Also which model variants were being routed?

katie (support): multiple customers reported increased 5xxs and truncated responses starting ~ 11:59 PST. I have a list of 4 high-traffic tenants (names redacted for privacy) where we saw spikes in error rate and user-facing dropped tokens. Support is triaging tickets.

jamal (eng-sre): grep output:```
$ jq '.request_meta | {id, model, max_tokens, final_length}' /var/log/gateway/requests.log | grep -E 'req_9f3a|req_ab12'
{ "id": "req_9f3a", "model": "longform-xxl", "max_tokens": null, "final_length": 114532 }
{ "id": "req_ab12", "model": "longform-xxl", "max_tokens": 200000, "final_length": 159223 }
```
so yeah — several requests either had explicit insane max_tokens or null (gateway allowed streaming until OOM).

maria (eng-runtime): ok immediate plan: 1) enforce a hard per-request token cap at the gateway (env var / filter) to stop any single request from allocating runaway seq length, 2) add a temporary model routing rule: divert longform-xxl to preemptible smaller-quantized variant (longform-xl-qd) for next 30m, 3) scale up decode pool by +2 nodes as a buffer, 4) enable denylist of clients that triggered > X OOMs for 1h while we investigate.

aj (oncall): doing hotfix 1 and 2 now. applying env override on deployment and patching routing.

aj (oncall): command I ran:```
kubectl set env deployment/decode-workers MAX_TOKENS_PER_REQUEST=4096 -n inference-prod
kubectl patch configmap/routing-rules -n inference-prod --type merge -p '{"data":{"longform-xxl":"longform-xl-qd"}}'
```
patch applied and new pods are rolling. ops-bot, please watch rollout.

ops-bot: Rollout started for deployment/decode-workers (replicas 24 -> 24). All pods are restarting one-by-one. 3 pods failed initial start due to OOM during warmup; they were auto-evicted and recreated. Rollout progress: 12/24 updated.

jamal (eng-sre): after the env change I'm seeing immediate drop in large token requests — telemetry shows tail of tokens_requested histogram moving left. OOM events dropping from 40/min to 3/min. still seeing some residual spikes from in-flight sessions.

maria (eng-runtime): can we also push a short-lived gateway validation to reject any request with max_tokens > 8192? do we have that route available via fast patch?

aj (oncall): pushed a quick Lua filter on envoy (hot reload) to enforce max_tokens <= 8192 and default to 1024 if null. code snippet:```
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local body = request_handle:body():getBytes(0, request_handle:body():length())
  local m = body and cjson.decode(body) or {}
  local mt = m["max_tokens"] or 1024
  if mt > 8192 then
    request_handle:respond({[":status"] = "400"}, "max_tokens exceeds temporary limit")
    return
  end
end
```
filter deployed to edge-gateway cluster.

jamal (eng-sre): metrics: OOMs down to 1-2/min, request error-rate down to baseline ~2.3%. customer impact metric: dropped requests window decreased by 92% after both fixes. support, can you confirm customer tickets are updating?

katie (support): ticket updates pushed: notified impacted customers about transient errors and mitigation steps. two customers asked for postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.

maria (eng-runtime): longer-term actions: - implement server-side token accounting that charges/limits before model allocation - add per-model soft quotas and a daily token budget guard - add test harness for malformed overrides + fuzzing to prevent bypasses - change routing policy to prefer quantized fallbacks automatically on OOM detection

aj (oncall): handing off to maria for broader follow-up and postmortem. I'll be available for escalation for 2h. Handoff notes: applied MAX_TOKENS_PER_REQUEST=4096, envoy filter rejecting >8192, temporary routing to longform-xl-qd, scaled decode pool +2. See runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/decode-oom.

maria (eng-runtime): acked handoff. will create incident postmortem and link to tickets. immediate triage items assigned: (1) gateway hard cap persisted in infra-as-code, (2) add unit tests for token header validation, (3) telemetry alert tuned to token_count histogram anomalies, (4) model config flag to refuse allocation if expected allocation > GPU free memory estimate.

incident-bot: Incident auto-closed (mitigated) at 2111111899. Severity downgraded to SEV3. Please attach postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:

jamal (eng-sre): quick notes for PM: root cause appears to be a client-visible change in a customer integration that started sending huge max_tokens in some bulk replay flows, and our gateway lacked a hard validation cap (only recommendations). We'll include reproduction steps and time-to-mitigate in the postmortem.

katie (support): updating customer comms summary and adding estimated impact window (11:59 PST - 12:12 PST). two high-tier customers saw ~30% request failures in the window.

maria (eng-runtime): creating postmortem draft and /assigning to jamal and aj for metrics and timeline.

aj (oncall): thanks all. leaving channel. :raised_hands:
